D.treatment: same curriculum filter applied to WeeBit

O.outcome_detail: retention of genuinely out-of-scope content after filtering

result.effect: 2.48% of 6,000 Beyond-K-5 passages retained; genuinely out-of-scope concepts identified in 3 passages (0.05%)

cells.quote: As an independent check, we apply the same pipeline to WeeBit [41], an external grade-labeled corpus (Figure 2, right). The filter retains 2.48% of 6,000Beyond-K–5passages; manual inspection identifies genuinely out-of-scope concepts in only three passages, corresponding to 0.05% of theBeyond-K–5split (the remaining content are web scraping artifacts, or content without educational value). We further conduct a corpus-wide scan using 126Beyond-K–5n-grams drawn from curriculum standards, finding matches in only 0.09% of retained passages.
cells.note: The study reports retention and manual inspection results for the filtered corpus, but does not explicitly report a randomized or controlled comparison design.

O.outcome_detail: retention of in-scope K–5 versus out-of-scope Beyond-K–5 content

cells.quote: The pipeline successfully reduces the retention ofBeyond-K–5content to 0% while preserving ~35% ofK–5(Figure 2, left).
cells.note: The study describes a precision-first filtering validation on CommonCoreText; it does not report random assignment, learner characteristics, setting, or duration.
